The short version

I'm a UI/UX designer with five years in the field, currently at NETGEAR. I work end-to-end — research, interaction, interface, and the unglamorous parts in between. I'm most useful early, when the real problem still needs framing, and late, when the small details decide whether a product feels trustworthy.

Comfortable owning a problem, showing my reasoning, and defending the trade-offs I made to get there. At NETGEAR I focus on on‑device LCDs for mobile routers, the web interfaces behind them, and the mobile apps that set them up.

At work

On a team I'm usually the one asking who we're actually building for, and whether the simplest version would do. I like systems but distrust sterility, so I'll argue for the one human detail that makes a product feel like it was made by a person.

I give direct feedback, kindly, and I take it the same way. And I'd rather remove a feature than decorate a broken one — restraint, for me, is a feature, not a limitation.

Outside work

Outside of design, I shoot film. It's a slower, more deliberate way of making images — and a good counterweight to working on screens all day. A few frames below.
